challenge.better_approach: Considered having _hold skip files the tester itself staged; that would hide the refused commit rather than fix it. Naming the paths is the shape every other commit in the house already takes (ticket 23c822fe8095).
challenge.hidden_assumption: That git commit -- <paths> with paths already staged commits exactly those paths. Measured: it is what every hand commit in this session does, and the hook sees next-index-<pid>.lock.
challenge.prior_art: Ticket 23c822fe8095 made the artifact check refuse a shared-index commit; ticket b0bb9743a5f4 made red_tickets ask the commons' own git. Its proof (cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_red_tickets_asks_the_commons_git_not_the_hooks.py) ran with no hook armed, which is why this slipped.
challenge.real_collision: None. Decision D7 of 207c4074b3d5 (stage by name, plain commit, no push) keeps its stage-by-name and no-push; only the commit names its paths, which the later 23c822fe8095 requires.

answers.falsifier: Under an armed path check in a scratch commons, a cast red commits with nothing left staged, and a second red after it casts and commits rather than being held.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator ruled the shape after I measured it 2026-11-16: both tester casts (f9c7ac6a69ba, 6fb272ba3d64) in /home/akien/dev/src/wt-ccr/CairnCommons were refused at commit by cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py check_shared_index
answers.how: red_tickets._commit already stages each named file; its commit step becomes `git commit -q -m <message> -- <named>`, which hands the hook git's --only temp index (next-index-*), the one check_shared_index admits. A red-first proof arms a scratch commons with that predicate as its pre-commit hook and casts one red, then two in sequence.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 and outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 (reds don't get lost): a red the tester measured must land as a committed ticket, not as staged dirt that also stops the next red from being ticketed.
answers.what: The tester's red cast commits by naming its paths, so the commons' path check passes it and the next red in the run casts instead of being held.

bullets.text: Every red the tester cast from a worktree was left staged and broke the run, because its commit did not name its paths; the next red then held instead of casting. Fixed by naming the paths.

title: The tester's red cast commits by naming its paths, so the commons' path check passes it and the next red in the run cast
